data.tittle: JOSE HOLGUIN-VERAS - The Quest for Sustainable Urban Logistics in an Era of Rapid (and Unpredictable) Technological and Economic Change
data.abstract: In this talk, Professor Holgu?n-Veras will discuss the challenges and opportunities presented by the rise of the internet and on-demand economy, and the development of novel vehicular technologies. These trends--from both the demand and supply sides--have led to significant increases in the number of freight deliveries and shipments made in urban areas; and to increase congestion, emissions, and conflicts with pedestrian and cyclists. The reactions to these effects on the part of various stakeholders have been mixed. Individuals seem to enjoy the new services provided. Users of transportation networks complain about the increasing freight traffic. Municipalities have, for the most part, decided not to interfere with these deployments. Freight carriers are both concerned by the challenges presented to them, and excited by the opportunities. In this talk, Professor Holgu?n-Veras will share his thoughts about how to make the most of these challenges and opportunities.
data.keywords: sustainable urban logistics technological economic
data.authors: Jose Holguin-Veras

data.tittle: Developments in City Logistics - The Path between Expectations and Reality
data.session: Freight Transportation and Urban Logistics I
data.abstract: Discussions in the context of city logistics relate to two areas, the supply of inner-city retail trade stores and service facilities as well as the delivery of parcels in the context of mail order and online retail business. These two problems must be considered separately due to the different requirements, even if at some points in the processes links can occur. However, the common problem is the increase in traffic congestion caused by delivery trips and the associated environmental impacts. The objective must be to find sustainable solutions to reduce these negative effects. Basis for this are, among others, a demand-oriented adaptation of the structures of the logistics facilities, improvements in routing, the use of new vehicle concepts and technologies as well as the expansion of real-time-based information management. We consider current developments and ideas regarding the two problems and related options and limitations. It turns out that not all solutions are effective and not necessarily sustainable. It is also unclear whether fundamental changes in economic and social structures will have far-reaching effects on future developments.
data.keywords: City logistics, Delivery concepts, New technologies
data.authors: Joachim R. Daduna

data.tittle: Measuring Environmental Impact of Collaborative Urban Transport Networks: A Case Study
data.session: Freight Transportation and Urban Logistics I
data.abstract: Nowadays, urban freight transport networks must be environmentally sustainable. As a consequence, collaboration strategies have been implemented as one alternative to enhance the efficiency of the supply chain and to reduce its environmental burden. However, there is a lack of knowledge about how to correctly quantify the environmental impact of collaborative urban freight transport networks. To fill this gap, we present an optimization approach for evaluating the environmental performance of collaborative systems by applying the Overall Greenness Performance (OGP) tool. We illustrate our approach using real data from the city of Bogot?, Colombia. Our results provide insights for shifting towards sustainable freight transportation networks. For example, we quantify savings up to 11% of CO2 emissions after applying collaboration in urban transportation contexts.
data.keywords: Urban freight transport, Collaboration, Environmental performance, Optimization, Urban logistics, Case study
data.authors: Andrés Muñoz-Villamizar, Elyn L. Solano-Charris, Javier Santos and Jairo R. Montoya-Torres

data.tittle: Using Advanced Information Systems to Improve Freight Efficiency: Results from a Pilot Program in Colombia
data.session: Freight Transportation and Urban Logistics I
data.abstract: The efficiency of the urban and inter-urban freight transport sector is crucial for Colombia?s economic competitiveness, and the government continually engages in projects to improve freight transport activities. Recently, as part of a program towards the reduction of greenhouse gases (GHGs) and the improvement of efficiency from the transportation sector, the Ministry of Transport pilot tested advanced information services using a freight brokerage system. This work discusses the results of this pilot program. Specifically, the work discusses the data collection methodology, provides details about the program, and describes the findings. The study had three stages. First, a socio-economic analysis of at least 500 vehicles/drivers, based on information from both vehicles and drivers. Second, the implementation of an ESD tool (Engine System Diagnostic Tool) device on the vehicle computer to measure some control variables of importance. Last, the data analysis of potential reduction on empty trips. The results show that the program can reduce the number of empty and non-revenue generating trips of the over-the-road freight transport (45% of trips in Colombia are empty) and improve the system. Specifically, the program reduced a third of these trips and generated new revenue trips to the participating carrier companies. However, the system reduced empty trips by 20%, and increased the number of trips per month, therefore, yielding more return on investment to drivers/vehicles and to the carrier.
data.keywords: Freight transport, freight brokerage, empty trips, compensated trips, Engine System Diagnostic Tool
data.authors: Adriana Moros-Daza, Daniela Cassandro-De La Hoz , Miguel Jaller-Martelo and Carlos D. Paternina-Arboleda

data.tittle: Allocation of Freight Externalities among Agents in the Supply Chain
data.session: Freight Transportation and Urban Logistics II
data.abstract:
This research is related to a crucial aspect of urban freight management, the impacts of the decisions made by agents in a supply chain on the generation of externalities. To analyze the effects of externalities, the inclusion of these in the costs of transportation is crucial. Yet, the discussion to who should pay for such increments remains unanswered. The analysis in this paper involves the development of a methodology based on cooperative game theory to obtain a fair allocation of the social cost generated by such decisions, including the private cost and externalities (i.e., CO2 emissions). 
To understand the externalities generated by freight activity, it is important to understand that freight is a result of an economic transaction from suppliers, freight carriers, and receivers. In equilibrium, their costs or benefits are reflected in the market prices they charge, and these are internalized by the participants in the transaction. Nevertheless, when an action of one or more agents impacts other agent not involved in the economic transaction then an externality is produced (e.g., congestion affects timing of passengers on the road, pollution affects health of pedestrians). Given that this externality is outside of the economic transaction, it is not internalized by the agents involved, thus its effects cannot be controlled. 
To eliminate externalities, Pigou (1920) proposed that pricing could be an effective mechanism, which created the foundation for the congestion pricing research. Although a substantial amount of research has followed on passenger-related congestion pricing, there is very little research on the use of pricing to eliminate or reduce freight externalities. The study of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey?s Time of Day Pricing Initiative and the resulting publications provide a direction to this research (Holgu?n-Veras et al., 2005; Holgu?n-Veras et al., 2006a; Holgu?n-Veras et al., 2006b) as it is the first systematic study of the real-life impacts of road pricing on freight traffic. Its findings concluded that time-of-day pricing failed to reduce freight traffic in a meaningful way. Thus to ensure a change in behavior, policy. 
The question that remains is: how to best allocate the costs to ensure that carriers change behavior in a way that is fair for them and for the other agents in the supply chain. To tackle this question, this research a methodology based on cooperative game theory to obtain a fair allocation of the social cost generated by the decisions of the key agents in the supply chain. This cost includes the private cost and externalities generated (i.e., CO2 emissions). Several scenarios related to the delivery decisions (time-of-day and shipment size) were developed and evaluated to obtain the allocation of social costs among the agents responsible for the decision. Results provide insight to a more effective allocation of incentives/penalties to reduce the externalities produced by freight.
data.keywords: Urban Freight Management, Externalities, Cooperative Game Theory?Supply Chain, Social Cost
data.authors: José Holguín-Veras, Diana Ramirez-Rios, Trilce Encarnación

data.tittle: Alternative Scenarios in Analyzing Florida?s Freight Imbalance
data.session: Freight Transportation and Urban Logistics II
data.abstract:
Florida struggles with a serious imbalance between inbound and outbound freight. With the third largest population in the U.S., the state offers a large and attractive consumer market. Statistics from the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) reveal that the total freight tonnage entering the state is nearly double the tonnage leaving the state. This imbalance suggests that many ships, containers, rail cars, and trucks leave the state empty or only partially loaded, which raises the cost for shippers and reduces the effectiveness of freight movements. One solution to this problem is for Florida seaports to secure a higher percentage of shipments bound for Florida markets.
Therefore, the major goal of this project was to evaluate opportunities to reduce the current inbound-outbound freight imbalance by increasing the percentage of imports consumed in Florida that enter the marketplace through Florida seaports and airports. To achieve this goal, the research team performed a multitude of different tasks in order to come up with an action plan to alleviate Florida?s freight imbalance. In return, the research team was able to determine specific scenarios where direct shipments to Florida has better results for landed times and landed costs for the shippers.
data.keywords: Freight Imbalance, Landed Cost, Landed Time
data.authors: Seckin Ozkul, Donna Davis, Abdul Pinjari, Iana Shaheen, Prachi Gupta

data.tittle: Math-heuristic for a Territory Design Problem
data.session: Freight Transportation and Urban Logistics II
data.abstract: In this work, we study a territory design problem. This type of problem consists of dividing a geographic area into territories that meet certain characteristics or planning criteria. The problem studied in this paper considers the division of a geographical area into compact, contiguous and balanced territories, with respect to one or several measures of activity. To ?nd feasible solutions for the problem, we propose a math-heuristic. The method ?rst constructs solutions, using a minisum objective as measure of dispersion, that are balanced with respect to the di?erent activity measures. Subsequently, the solutions are modi?ed so that they satisfy the contiguity constraints. To test the performance of the proposed method, we use a set of test instances available in the literature. The results obtained are compared with the optimal solutions of the test instances. According to this comparison, the proposed method provides optimal solutions or solutions very close to the optimal solution with a reasonable computational e?ort compared to that required by an exact solution method.
data.keywords: Territory design problem ? p-median ? GRASP ? Mathheuristic
data.authors: Mario A. Solana, Juan A. Díaz and Dolores E. Luna

data.tittle: Caribbean Ports, Inland Logistics, and the Panama Canal Expansion: a Mode and Port Choice Analysis
data.session: Freight Transportation and Urban Logistics III
data.abstract: This paper develops an international freight transport model for predicting the importers? behavior in the port/path-choice decisions after the Panama Canal expansion. A real-data case study for Colombian ports was developed assuming that the expansion will reduce the time to cross the canal. Two infrastructure investment projects of the Colombian government were evaluated as likely scenarios. Results show the adequacy of the model for its predictive purpose and its usability to carry sensitivity analyses of scenarios. The overriding outcome is that the model could guide governmental decisions on the infrastructures domain by demonstrating their effect in the logistic realm.
data.keywords: International freight transport; Port choice; Multimodal network; Discrete choice models; Infrastructure decisions
data.authors: Gomez-Jacome Nicolas, Garcia-Llinas Guisselle, Paternina-Arboleda Carlos D and Jaller-Martelo Miguel

data.tittle: Proposing solutions to create service classes and identifying groups of routine riders in bike sharing systems
data.session: Freight Transportation and Urban Logistics III
data.abstract: This research presents a bike itinerary choice model for a bike sharing system (BSS). Machine learning techniques are used to characterize the bike itineraries within a given day. We present a method to detect the ?most faithful? users with respect to itinerary types and a Bayesian network model which emphasizes the link between the conditions with which the itinerary is chosen and the itinerary type. In considering the expansion of large bike sharing systems, we focus on the problem of supply chain management for delivering the service. The model has a data driven exploratory phase made with python on real-world data, initially 11,771,185 records of bike sharing journeys made in Milan between 2015 and 2019. Solutions can be provided for the adoption of pricing strategies, the use of different payment supports for renting the bicycle, also service innovation with the expansion of the offer by number and type of accessible vehicles. In order to be able to model the user's needs, we propose a solution to create service classes and one to form groups of routine riders, who observe similar routes with a constant frequency over time. To this end we consider two virtual issues at the same time: to guarantee service levels aiming at satisfying the contract level agreements to perform the function of a public transport service provider and possibly to endow the service quality across a heterogeneous user base to respond to the greater number of requests coming from real and potential customers who want to use the bicycle to get around the congested traffic of the city center
data.keywords: Bike Sharing, Transport, Machine Learning Techniques, Service Quality, User?s Classes, Itinerary
data.authors: Giorgio Saibene, Sabrina Gaito, Gianzarlo Manzi, Silvia Salini & Matteo Zignani

data.tittle: Forecast of bicycle traffic flows within complex public transport circuits
data.session: Freight Transportation and Urban Logistics III
data.abstract:
Metropolitan areas in Europe tend to grow both in size and number. They are defined hubs of government, commerce and transportation by the United Nation, places where the resident population has almost doubled in the last twenty years. 
The people need to better share spaces and to move, has seen the creation of new and sometimes the revisiting of traditional transport systems. For example, bike sharing sistems have proliferated all over the world and have attracted the attention of large private transport players such as Uber as well as Chinese institutional investors supported by companies the likes of Alibaba Group Holding. 
Bike sharing systems play a central role in what is identified to be one of the six pillars of a smart city: smart mobility. Key trends in urbanization likely to unfold over the coming years is crucial to the implementation of new housing and living patterns in metropolitan areas, promoted by a system of private and public interests and investments, made by financial institutions and the state bureaucracy. 
A Bayesian model for the analysis of flow counts is based on a network journeys data of the bike sharing platform of Milan, BikeMi. The Incorporating edge-specific covariates, we assume a zero-inflated Poisson mixture regression model, which easily accommodates for the sparse nature of the network under investigation. 
Not only traffic volumes, but also environmental variables, meteorological indicators and existing public transport systems hubs can influence traffic. This leads to a first understanding and definition of the problem of bicycle traffic formation in city centre, monitored by time slots and type of days of the week. 
Subsequently, the results of the Poisson regression model can be applied to a coherent logistic management of the city transport service. 
The latest subject leads to predicting and improving smart mobility with a robust model-based approach. The aim of the research is to predicting the occurrence of situations in which a bike station is either empty or full, thus possibly creating demand loss and customer dissatisfaction. Experiments on BikeMi stations located in the central area of Milan can be provided to underline the benefits of the proposed methods.
data.keywords: Bike sharing, Transport, Bayesian model, Heuristic method for logistic management
data.authors: Giorgio Saibene

data.tittle: Greedy Heuristic for the Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows, Synchronization constraints and Heterogeneous Fleet
data.abstract: This paper focuses on a new variant of the Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows and Synchronization constraints (VRPTWSyn), inspired by a routing problem faced by the oil & gas industry. Here, a heterogeneous fleet of Anchor Handling Tug Supply vessels (AHTS) must be assigned to perform tasks at offshore platforms, and most tasks require the simultaneous action of more than two tugs. Instances are proposed, as well as a greedy randomized heuristic that generates feasible solutions to the problem. As shown by the computational experiments reported here, although the complexity of the AHTS-routing problem is higher than the VRPTWSyn, the proposed method could produce a diverse set of feasible solutions, which in the future may be improved by a meta-heuristic-based algorithm.
data.keywords: Anchor Handling Tug Supply, Vehicle Routing Problem, Synchronization, Greedy Heuristic, Oil & gas
data.authors: Luísa Brandão Cavalcanti and André Bergsten Mendes

data.tittle: Optimal solutions for the vehicle routing problem with split demands
data.abstract: This paper describes a branch-and-cut algorithm for a generalization of the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem where a customer can be visited several times. The algorithm is based on solving a Mixed Integer Programming model for a relaxed problem, and a cutting-plane procedure to eliminate invalid integer solutions. Computational results on benchmark instances show the performance of the algorithm compared with other approaches found in the literature. In particular, the new algorithm is able to solve a testbed SDVRP instance that was unsolved in the literature.
data.keywords: Capacitated Vehicle Routing ? Split Demand ? Branch-and-cut
data.authors: Hipólito Hernández-Pérez and Juan-José Salazar-González

data.tittle: The one-commodity pickup and delivery vehicle routing problem: A mixed-integer linear programming approach
data.abstract: In this paper we study the one-commodity pickup and delivery vehicle routing problem. It aims to design a set of routes able to pick up or delivery a known amount of a single product supplied or demanded by two different types of locations (pickup or delivery nodes). To do so, a capacitated fleet of homogeneous vehicles is available to meet the demand while the total traveling cost is minimized. However, when several vehicles are available, optimal routes for the problem are not typically cost-balanced. Therefore, we propose a mixed-integer linear program to model the one-commodity pickup and delivery vehicle routing problem with length route constraints and we compare the performance and balance for different length parameters. To solve this mathematical model, we use a commercial solver, we test instances with up to 40 nodes and different target values for balancing routes. Finally, we provide some insights about how the number of nodes, number of vehicles and vehicle capacity affect imbalance throughout the route costs.
data.keywords: Pickup and Delivery, Mixed-integer linear programming, Vehicle routing problem
data.authors: Juan David Palacio, Juan Carlos Rivera

data.tittle: A MILP Model and a GRASP Algorithm for the Helicopter Routing Problem with Multi-trips and Time Windows
data.abstract: This work presents a new mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model and a GRASP algorithm for the Helicopter Routing Problem (HRP) with multi-trips and time windows. The HRP consists of serving a set of transportation requests, de?ned as a pair of boarding and landing locations, where helicopters are used as transportation mode. This novel model incorporates the characteristics present in routing helicopters for o?shore platforms and, also, a new set of constraints is proposed to handle an issue unnoticed so far for the HRP: o?shore platforms can be visited by helicopters one at a time. The main goal of the presented HRP is to minimize the cost of meeting the set of transportation requests. We provide computational experiments for well-known instances available in the literature with up to 80 requests. On average, our GRASP algorithm is capable to solve all instances, whereas CPLEX found solutions only for small instances, lower bounds for small to medium instances and no lower bounds for medium to large instances.
data.keywords: Helicopter Routing Problem ? GRASP ? O?shore Platforms Logistics
data.authors: André Manh˜aes Machado, Geraldo Regis Mauri, Maria Claudia Silva Boeres and Rodrigo de Alvarenga Rosa

data.tittle: Metaheuristics for Generalised Periodic Electric Vehicle Routing Problem
data.abstract: This paper presents the Generalized Periodic Electric Vehicle Routing Problem, named GPEVRP, which is an extension of the Periodic Electric Vehicle Routing Problem (PEVRP) proposed in previous research. The GPEVRP is de?ned by a planning horizon of several periods typically ?days?, with the constraints that each customer must be visited a required number of times, which must be related to a pattern, that is, a combination of days chosen among a set of allowed combinations of days, must be satis?ed every time by its required demand, and that a limited ?eet of electric vehicles (EVs) available each day at the depot must be respected. The EVs could be charged during their trips at the depot and in the available external charging stations. The objective of the GPEVRP is to minimize the total cost of routing and charging over the time horizon. We propose three metaheuristics to solve the problem. The ?rst two methods are global approaches, allow solving simultaneously the planning level (pattern assignment) and the operational level (routing and charging). These methods are Large Neighbourhood Search (LNS) and Adaptive Large Neighbourhood Search (ALNS) for which we have proposed a new metric for the selection of patterns. The third method is a two-phase approach, called Multi-start Guided LNS, for which a perturbation phase changes the pattern and manages the planning level, and an intensi?cation phase based on LNS optimizes the operational level and guides the perturbation through a memory. The results show that a simple global approach such as LNS leads to better results on a very constraining problem such as the problem of our study.
data.keywords: Periodic vehicle routing, electric vehicle, charging station, large neighborhood search, adaptive large neighborhood search
data.authors: Tayeb Oulad Kouider, Wahiba Ramdane Cherif-Khettaf, and Ammar Oulamara

data.tittle: Electric Bus Scheduling and Optimal Charging
data.abstract: In this paper, we study an operational problem of optimizing the deployment of electric buses in an urban public transport service. We propose a modeling aimed at optimizing the assignment of buses to line services of a public transport network, then the allocation of parking places to buses taking into account the typology of depots and ?nally the optimization of bus charging while complying with technical constraints. The model is based and tested on a concrete case study of a public transport company. The results show that optimization models can address the weaknesses of electric buses, namely limited range and long charging times, and thus provide public transport organizations with bus use strategies and bus charging policies.
data.keywords: Electric buses, charging, scheduling, MILP, heuristics
data.authors: Bilal Messaoudi and Ammar Oulamara

data.tittle: A Two-Pheromone Trail Ant Colony System Approach for the Heterogeneous Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows, Multiple Products and Product Incompatibility
data.abstract: We consider a variant of the vehicle routing problem subject to time windows for every customer, multiple products and incompatibility between them, using a heterogeneous ?eet of vehicles. Since the problem is NP-hard, the approach to achieve feasible solutions is an ant colony system with two-pheromone to minimize routing cost and vehicle ?eet size. Experiments conducted using instances from the literature show that the proposed approach provides competitive solutions in relatively short computational times.
data.keywords: Vehicle Routing ? Time Windows ? Multiple Products ? Compatibility Constraints ? Ant Colony System
data.authors: Andres Palma-Blanco, Esneyder Rafael González, and Carlos D. Paternina-Arboleda

data.tittle: The Consistent Vehicle Routing Problem for a Food Distribution Firm
data.abstract:
In this work, we present a heuristic for solving The Consistent Vehicle Routing Problem (ConVRP), which is motivated by a real-world application in a distribution center of a food company. The problem is characterized by a set of customers that vary from day to day, as well as their demand. Additionally, each customer requires that their orders be delivered within a certain time window. The main difficulty of the problem comes from the large size of instances and high demand variability. 
We propose a new heuristic for solving the ConVRP for the food company. For evaluating the performance of the heuristic, we used the benchmark instances generated for the ConVRP from the literature. The results confirm the good performance of the implemented heuristic, outperforming several instances. Finally, for the food company, we obtain significant improvements in terms of generating a better consistent service.
data.keywords: Consistent vehicle routing, heuristics, logistics
data.authors: Hernán Lespay, Karol Sucha

data.tittle: Formulation for the problem of median tour generalized with cumulative time
data.abstract:
In this work we define and propose a formulation for the problem of median tour generalized with cumulative time (GMTPL). This problem arises as an extension of the median tour problem (MTP) proposed by Current and Schilling (1994), where it is sought to find a tour of p nodes, so that the rest of the nodes of the graph are assigned to a node of the tour. The MTP is a multi-objective problem, since it seeks to optimize the cost of the tour and the associated allocation times. 

In the GMTPL the graph is divided into clusters and each node belongs to only one cluster. This problem, like the MTP, is classified as a multi-objective problem, due to the fact that it seeks to optimize the cost of the route and the accumulated time of permanence in the tour. 

The GMTPL can be used as an alternative for the logistics of passenger transportation, where a balance between the cost of the route and the quality of the service is sought.
data.keywords: Multi-Objective Problem, Routing, Operations research, Mathematical programming
data.authors: Alex Barrales, Carlos Obreque

data.tittle: MIGUEL JALLER - Changes in the Retail and Distribution Landscape: Behavioral and Logistics Modeling Implications
data.abstract: In recent years, the rapid adoption of omni-channel distribution strategies has dramatically changed how we shop and the way companies design their retail and distribution operations. All these changes have important implications for logistics modeling from the strategic, tactical and operational perspectives. This presentation discusses the implications for assessing the shopping demand and logistics decisions under this dynamic environment. Specifically, Dr. Jaller will discuss changes in shopping decisions, from where to shop, what to shop, and how much to shop. The presentation will also provide an overview of the impacts of and tradeoffs between facility location, fleet and technology characteristics, time-windows, and the use of crowd-shipping services. Moreover, Dr. Jaller will cover the impacts from these decisions when thinking about the sustainability of the urban transportation system with respect to travel activity and emissions.
data.keywords: retail distribution logistics modeling
data.authors: Miguel Jaller

data.tittle: An event driven architecture for a real-time data exchange platform for the RORO transportation in the Baltic region
data.abstract:
To optimize and secure the overall transportation, a coherent information and collaboration regarding the different artefacts in the logistics domain is essential. Many solutions for improving logistics processes have been developed in recent years. However, an integrating platform and organization among different stakeholders is missing. In this talk, we present a platform design that aims to improve collaboration among logistics partners, especially for the Baltic region RORO network. Our platform allows to share data in real-time enhancing the collaboration among different logistic partners thus optimizing the transportation for RORO logistics in the Baltic region. 

Based on comprehensive studies of the RORO segment we identified the presence of mostly proprietary systems communicating in a bilateral fashion as today's main drawback for an overall data exchange. Thus, we designed a single, distributed, service-oriented platform allowing (third-party) services to be integrated and communicating by two main communication schemes, event streams and client-server-queries. Each artifact participating in the platform has unique identifications, i.e. users have a unique id and single-sign-on and services are signed after validation by the platform operators. An access management system controls the rights of services and users to data etc. For establishing business models the platform provides detailed accounting capabilities. 

From our investigations we learned that events drive the logistics ecosystem, especially the one of port terminals. While the RORO cargo transportation is a continuous process its behaviour can be described and controlled adequately with associated event streams. Every actor in the logistics chain owns a part of information about the cargo transported and may contribute this information using the publish and subscribe pattern via event streams to interested parties, respecting access control. Event streaming allows to achieve a (soft) real-time information exchange and may trigger further services, for example to integrate synchromodal planning continuously optimizing the route. 

Exchange of complex but well-structured data is ensured via traditional client-server-based, SQL-style queries. 

Services, e.g. developed by third parties, may enrich the functionality of the platform and have to follow typical cloud based design to ensure an overall robustness and the scalable operation of the platform.

Currently, the platform is under development
data.keywords: Last generation ICT networks, ICT systems for port communities, Port smart logistics, Multi-agent system in logistics, Internet of things on smart logistics
data.authors: Karam Kharraz, Martin Leucker, Maria Ostanina

data.tittle: A Decomposed Fourier-Motzkin Elimination Framework to Derive Vessel Capacity Models
data.abstract: Accurate Vessel Capacity Models (VCMs) expressing the trade-o? between di?erent container types that can be stowed on container vessels are required in core liner shipping functions such as uptake-, capacity-, and network management. Today, simple models based on volume, weight, and refrigerated container capacity are used for these tasks, which causes overestimations that hamper decision making. Though previous work on stowage planning optimization in principle provide ?negrained linear Vessel Stowage Models (VSMs), these are too complex to be used in the mentioned functions. As an alternative, this paper contributes a novel framework based on Fourier-Motzkin Elimination that automatically derives VCMs from VSMs by projecting unneeded variables. Our results show that the projected VCMs are reduced by an order of magnitude and can be solved 20-34 times faster than their corresponding VSMs with only a negligible loss in accuracy. Our framework is applicable to LP models in general, but are particularly e?ective on block-angular structured problems such as VSMs. We show similar results for a multi-commodity ?ow problem.
data.keywords: Fourier-Motzkin Elimination?Vessel Capacity Model?Liner Shipping ? Projection
data.authors: Mai L. Ajspur, Rune M. Jensen, and Kent H. Andersen

data.tittle: Estimating Discharge Time of Cargo Units ? A Case of Ro-Ro Shipping
data.abstract: Ro-Ro shipping is a dominant form of short sea freight transport. Ro-Ro ship operators are today unable to provide customers with precise information about when trailers are available for pick-up by customers on the terminal despite vessel arrival times being well known in due time. This results in reduced truck utilization, longer waiting time for drivers, less efficient yard space utilization, potential terminal congestion and dissatisfied customers. In this paper the cargo unit discharge time estimation problem of Ro-Ro shipping is solved in collaboration with a European short-sea Ro-Ro shipping company. A module-based framework using statistical analysis for estimating the discharge time is proposed and tested. The initial framework is able to estimate the earliest pick-up time of each individual truck or trailer within 1 hour accuracy for up to 70% of all cargo. The results of the study show potential for improving performance and accuracy. Further investigation and testing is currently ongoing by the case company based on the results from this study.
data.keywords: Cargo Discharge Time Estimation, Short Sea Shipping, Terminal Operations, Integrated Logistics Chain, Industry Implementation.
data.authors: Beizhen Jia, Niels Gorm Rytter, Line Blander Reinhardt, Gauvain Haulot and Mads Bentzen Billesø

data.tittle: Port Community System Adoption: Game Theoretic Framework For an Emerging Economy Case Study
data.abstract: Port community systems (PCS), as platforms for connecting the stakeholders of a port community (PC), build a basis for improving information exchange. These systems support automation and visibility along global supply chains, thereby helping to enhance the overall PC performance in both local and foreign trade activities. However, successful real-world PCS adoption often involves multiple collaborating parties interacting with at least two di?erent types of PC stakeholders. This study assesses the payo? of the alliances between three types of stakeholders to ensure the adoption of a PCS. In order to accomplish the former, it also identi?es the di?erent possible collaborations at the inception of a PCS. We use di?erent simulated scenarios to obtain the expected payo? of each stakeholder, in terms of lead time savings achieved, and based on the Shapley value method allocate pro?ts to each coalition. Also, we present a sensitivity analysis to test each coalition with di?erent variation of the market while adopting a PCS. The main result is that pro?ts gained from the adoption of a PCS funded by the port community grand coalition are higher than those from pairs or individual members. Also, the pro?ts gained from the coalition of two cooperative members are higher than any individual e?ort. Therefore, the stakeholders? individual incentive to join a PCS coalition should be relatively high coming from a steady coalition.
data.keywords: port community system, game theory, Shapley value, pro?t allocation
data.authors: Adriana Moros-Daza, René Amaya-Mier, Guisselle Garcia-Llinas, and Stefan Voß

data.tittle: Towards a Semantic Intelligence to Support Seaport Governance in Environmental and Ecological Sustainability
data.abstract: Taking into account that seaport governance in environmental and ecological sustainability becomes a seaport function of growing public interest, environmental and ecological factors are criteria that will enter into operational choices, capital investments, and cargo routing decisions. Environmental influences as well as factors of institutional governance (regulations and environmental management practices) may lead to common interests among the members. We propose the use of a semantic-based approach to further look at how the knowledge needed to understand the effects observed in seaport decision-making tackle the difficulty of sharing information and finding the best possible representations (model) in order to aid collective decision-making process. The benefits of the semantic use of terminology relevant for the port governance are envisaged in which modeling an ontology will require consensus among domain experts from many and different port areas and the complexity of reaching consensus when multiple conflicting views may exist can threaten consistency across the systems.
data.keywords: seaport governance, semantic intelligence, environmental and ecological Sustainability
data.authors: Ana X. HALABI-ECHEVERRY, Juan Carlos VERGARA-SILVA, German A. ORTIZ-BASTO

data.tittle: Estimating the Impact of Trade Facilitation in Regional Supply Chains: a Case Study in Colombia
data.abstract: This paper shows how the use of a supply chain perspective allows for better estimation and evaluation of the impact of trade policies on the economy. This paper is based on the modeling framework proposed by Blanco et. al (2015) which estimates costs related to international trade for buyers and sellers, this paper analyzes extensive data from 16 economic sectors in Colombia to estimate the impact of modeling trade facilitation under a supply chain framework. Among the findings, this paper estimates the impact of trade to be 11.8 % of the total trade volume. The model is also used to evaluate the potential impact of 9 different trade policies, highlighting the importance of investing in in-country transportation to improve supply chain competitiveness. It is noticeable that for one scenario on improved payment terms the total global logistics cost did not show better results. On the other hand, the improvement in the cost of capital, the total savings are not relevant. The practical implications involve the modeling framework and results provide the evidence for making the necessary changes on the meso-economic economic policies, In order to focus on the appropriate investments on logistics infrastructure, technology and logic for the improvement on the international of the regional economy. Finally, This paper enhances previous research on trade facilitation and evaluates a global supply trade cost function on a vast sample of Colombia?s import/export products. To the best of the authors? knowledge, this modeling framework applied to an emerging economy has not been implemented yet on a regional (meso-economic) basis, Furthermore, the scenario planning structure used in this paper is novel. The information was gathered from directly declared preferences from participating firms in the study and other parameters defined by the authors.
data.keywords: Trade Facilitation, Regional supply chains, Logistics trade policies, Competitiveness, Global supply chain cost, Emerging economies
data.authors: Carlos D. Paternina-Arboleda, Daniel Orlando Rivera

data.tittle: A Note on Alternative Objectives for the Blocks Relocation Problem
data.abstract: The Blocks Relocation Problem (BRP) is an important problem arising at container terminals when containers have to be transshipped. Recently, we have seen the upcoming discussion whether some objectives are more appropriate than others. While most authors minimize the number of relocations as objective, some minimize the crane?s working time. After adapting a given BRP formulation by including the second objective in two variants, a computational study is carried out on benchmark instances from literature applying some sensitivity analysis indicating to which extent optimal solutions change if the objective is replaced. If the number of relocations is minimized, often larger crane working times may be obtained. Conversely, if the crane working time is minimized, often solutions achieving also a minimum number of relocations are found. Based on our analysis, the consideration of alternative objectives like crane working time is recommended.
data.keywords: Container relocation, port operations, integer programming, crane working time, blocks relocation problem
data.authors: Stefan Voß and Silvia Schwarze

data.tittle: BENJAMIN HAZEN - Supply Chain Management at the International-Level: How Computational Logistics Scholars Might Contribute
data.abstract: Supply chain management activities are conducted in and serve nearly every region of the globe. The interdependences created via these ubiquitous and increasingly global trade relationships command the need for more attention on the international-level of supply chain management. However, most supply chain research is conducted at the organizational-level, with very few studies considering a supply chain-level of analysis. To date, the body of knowledge on national and international perspectives of global trade is found in policy, strategy, government, international relations, defense, and other journals and magazines primarily grounded in the social sciences. This talk will describe some of these international-level supply chain management issues. It will also discuss needs and opportunities for transdisciplinary collaboration seeking to solve international-level SCM problems like sustainability.
data.keywords: sustainability computational logistics supply chain international-level global

data.tittle: A facility allocation-location approach to analyze the capability of the state-owned Mexican petroleum company to respond to the closure of pipelines
data.abstract: In recent years, Mexico has reported signiﬁcant economic losses caused by the organized theft of gasoline at diﬀerent stages of the supply chain of its national petroleum company. As measure against these actions, the government ordered the speciﬁc closure of distribution pipelines between reﬁneries and storage depots. However, this led to large shortage of gasoline and economic losses in the south central region of Mexico, even though distribution through tanker trucks was increased. Thus, the response capability of the company must be analyzed to quantitatively assess the shortage risk and propose alternatives if such disruption happens again. The present work addresses this task through a facility allocation-location approach where the location of additional storage depots was considered. For this analysis, the most updated data regarding the locations of gasoline storage depots and stations was used. Also, due to the large size of this data, the results of this approach were obtained through the development of a hybrid meta-heuristic. The results support the increase of storage depots to reduce the shortage risk and the service distance. This corroborates the public discussion that distribution of gasoline is restricted by the current infrastructure and that additional storage depots are needed. This infrastructure can also provide more control to reduce gasoline theft.
data.keywords: Gasoline Stations Capacitated Facility Location Problem Location-Allocation Heterogeneous Capacity
data.authors: Santiago Omar Caballero Morales and Jose Luis Martinez Flores

data.tittle: Integrated Production Lot Size and Distribution Planning with SharedWarehouses
data.abstract: Collaboration in supply chains (SCs) is steadily improving especially due to advanced information systems that provide transparency over resource allocation, utilization, and dynamic demands.Weare examining the caseof shared inventory spaces in SCs where utilization of storage spaces depend on all SC partners. Decisions that need to be made are when to produce how much of multiple products and where and how long to store them in order to ful?ll known customer demands.Therefore,we take production, inventory control and placement, as well as distribution (logistics) decisions into consideration. Special emphasis is made on setup considerations for detailed production sequencing. We analyze this integrated approach that leads to reduced overall SC costs and extends the literature to the view of shared resources that become increasingly prominent with the developments of Industry 4.0. solutions.
data.keywords: supply chain, lot-size, distribution, planning, shared warehouses
data.authors: Julia Pahl

data.tittle: Production and inventory planning in meal-kit industry
data.abstract: Production planning in food processing industry requires simultaneously lost sizing and scheduling of multiple products. In this talk, we present one such problem involving multiple setups including sequence-dependent setups. A problem specific mathematical programming heuristic is developed to improve the lower bound and reduce the MIP solve time. Numerically study based on realistic data sets will be presented to demonstrate the efficiency of the approach.
data.keywords: Production planning, MIP, Heuristic, Scheduling, Lot-size
data.authors: Satyaveer Chauhan

data.tittle: A stochastic, Multi-Commodity Multi-Period Inventory-Location Problem: Modeling and Solving an Industrial Application
data.abstract: This paper addresses the real-world supply chain network design problem with a strategic multi-commodity and multi-period inventory-location problem with stochastic demands. The proposed methodology involves a complex non-linear, non-convex, mixed integer programming model, which allows for the optimization of warehouse location, demand zone?s assignment, and manufacturing settings while minimizing the fixed costs of a distribution center (DC), along with the transportation and inventory costs in a multi-commodity, multi-period scenario. In addition, a genetic algorithm is implemented to obtain near-optimal solutions at competitive times. We applied the model to a real-world industrial case of a Colombian rolled steel manufacturing company, where a new, optimized supply chain distribution network is required to serve customers at a national level. The proposed approach provides a practical solution to optimize their distribution network, achieving significant cost reductions for the company.
data.keywords: supply chain network design; inventory location problems; facility location problems; genetic algorithms, safety stock, cycle stock, explicit enumeration, stochastic modelling
data.authors: Mauricio Orozco-Fontalvo, and Víctor Cantillo, Pablo A. Miranda

data.tittle: Emergency service in electric utility: A Case Study in Rio de Janeiro
data.abstract: The ability of power systems to maintain stability and to ensure continuous supply of electrical power to customers in the event of a disturbance is of critical importance. Failures in the system can strongly affect educational in-stitutions, business establishments, and human health, such as in hospitals. Due to the consequences of a blackout in power system grid, the electric utilities usually has expert teams who are responsible to repair a failure has soon as possible. Therefore, vehicles location is one of the critical factors that determine the efficiency of power system emergency repair. This paper examines the emergency repair service in electrical system, using the case study of the Brazilian Electric Utility responsible for providing energy to over than 10 million people in Rio de Janeiro state. The objective of the study is to identify the best positions (guard stations) for service vehicles in order to maximize coverage (MCLP model) and reduce the total distance traveled by the vehicles (p-median model) to answer the calls of the con-sumers of power grid repair. The set of candidate points for guard stations was determined using a Voronoi diagram. Our results showed in the cases where unplanned power outages are geographic dispersed; the guard stations selected by MCLP and p-median are very close, indicating that there is a convergence of the two models results.
data.keywords: MCLP, P-median, Voronoi Diagram, Power System Emergency
data.authors: Marcelle Cordeiro, Pedro Basilio, Eduardo Rabello, Fabrício Nunes, Lino Marujo

data.tittle: Route overlap addition metrics for order batching on a unidirectional cyclical picking line
data.abstract:
An order picking system with a unidirectional cyclical picking line is extended to include order batching. Batches must be formed to minimise walking distance that is measured as the total number of cycles traversed by the pickers in the picking line. This picking system shows some similarities to a unidirectional carousel. Three metrics are introduced that add information about possible route overlap of orders in a batch to approximate walking distance before picker routing. These metrics thus identify potentially compatible orders. The section of the picking line that is traversed to pick an order is called the span of that order. Within a span a picker must stop at a subset of locations to perform a physical pick. The stops-non-identical spans, the non-identical stops-spans and the stops-spans ratio metric are introduced. On the basis of these route overlap addition metrics different solution approaches are tested to form batches. The best combination of route overlap addition metric and solution approach is found in a numerical experiment using real life data of 50 sample picking lines from a distribution centre of a prominent South African retailer. Batches are restricted to two orders per batch due to a size restriction on the picking device. The usability of route overlap addition metrics
as approximations for walking distance before picker routing is confirmed by the results. The combination of stops-non-identical spans metric and greedy smallest entry heuristic generate the best results. Furthermore, the idea of a nearest two ending heuristic is proposed in which two orders of a batch do not have to start and end at the same location resulting in a hard bound for the minimum number of total
cycles traversed.
data.keywords: order batching, route overlap addition metrics, unidirectional cyclical picking line, unidirectional carousel systems
data.authors: Flora Hofmann, Stephan Visagie

data.tittle: Developing an Effective Decomposition-Based Procedure for Solving the Quadratic Assignment Problem
data.abstract: The quadratic assignment problem is about designing the best layouts for facilities and has a wide variety of applications in industry. This paper presents a decomposition-based procedure for solving this NP-hard optimization problem. The procedure aims at enhancing an initial solution in ?ve interacting and synergetic layers. In the ?rst layer, the initial solution undergoes the process of local search and becomes local optimal. In the second layer, the linear assignment technique is called and results in a suggestion for an enhancement. The third layer is involved with decomposing the proposed suggestion into several cycles. Then, in the fourth layer, each cycle is further decomposed into several segments. The number of the segments associated with each cycle is the length of the corresponding cycle, calculated in the third layer. Finally, the segments are processed in the ?fth layer and potentially enhance the original solution. The employed decomposition has proved to be very e?ective, and comparing the performance of the procedure with that of other state-of-the-art procedures indicates its e?ciency.
data.keywords: metaheuristics ? local searches ? decomposition-based techniques ? facility layout ? quadratic assignment ? linear assignment
data.authors: Mehrdad Amirghasemi and Reza Zamani

data.tittle: Optimization of the P-Hub Median Problem via Artificial Immune Systems
data.abstract: Recent advances in logistics, transportation and in telecommunications o?er great opportunities to citizens and organizations in a globally-connected world, but they also arise a vast number of complex challenges that decision makers must face. In this context, a popular optimization problem with practical applications to the design of hub-andspoke networks is analyzed: the Uncapacitated Single Allocation p-Hub Median Problem (USApHMP) where a ?xed number of hubs have unlimited capacity, each non-hub node is allocated to a single hub and the number of hubs is known in advance. An immune inspired metaheuristic is proposed to solve the problem in deterministic scenarios. In order to show its e?ciency, a series of computational tests are carried out using small and large size instances from the Australian Post dataset with node sizes up to 200. The results contribute to a deeper understanding of the e?ectiveness of the employed metaheuristic for solving the USApHMP in small and large networks.
data.keywords: Arti?cial Immune Systems?p-Hub Median Problem?Metaheuristics ? CLONALG.
data.authors: Stephanie Alvarez Fernandez, Gabriel Lins e Nobrega and Daniel G. Silva

data.tittle: A Decision Support Tool for Energy-Optimising Railway Timetables Based on Behavioural Data
data.session: Selected Topics in Decision Support Systems and ICT Tools I
data.abstract: Energy-e?cient train operation can reduce operating costs and contribute to a reduction in CO2 emissions. To utilise the full potential of energy-e?cient driving, energy-e?cient timetabling is crucial. To address this problem, we propose a decision support tool to give timetable planners insight into energy consumption for a given timetable. The decision support tool uses a recommendation based on quadratic optimisation of a given timetable. Di?erently to previous work, the optimisation uses actual data from the train operation, which is pre-processed by data reduction, outlier detection, and second-degree regression modelling. With this approach, our results show that the optimised timetables can save up to 33.07% energy on a single section and up to 6.23% for a complete timetable. Solutions are computed in less than a microsecond.
data.keywords: Energy-e?cient, train, timetabling, Decision support, Data mining , Quadratic optimisation
data.authors: Mathias Bejlegaard Madsen, Matthias Villads Hinsch Als, Rune M. Jensen, and Sune Edinger Gram

data.tittle: Evaluation of Bottom-up and Top-down Strategies for Aggregated Forecasts: State Space Models and ARIMA Applications
data.session: Selected Topics in Decision Support Systems and ICT Tools I
data.abstract: In this research, we consider monthly series from the M4 competition to study the relative performance of top-down and bottom-up strategies by means of implementing forecast automation of state space and ARIMA models. For the bottom-up strategy, the forecast for each series is developed individually and then these are combined to produce a cumulative forecast of the aggregated series. For the top-down strategy, the series or components values are first combined and then a single forecast is determined for the aggregated series. Based on our implementation, state space models showed a higher forecast performance when a top-down strategy is applied. ARIMA models had a higher forecast performance for the bottom-up strategy. For state space models the top-down strategy reduced the overall error significantly. ARIMA models showed to be more accurate when forecasts are first determined individually. As part of the development we also proposed an approach to improve the forecasting procedure of aggregation strategies.
data.keywords: decision support systems , ICT tools, State space Models, ARIMA Applications
data.authors: Milton Soto-Ferrari, Odette Chams-Anturi, Juan P. Escorcia-Caballero, Namra Hussain, and Muhammad Khan

data.tittle: Developing Logistic Software Platforms: E-Market Place, a Case of Study
data.session: Selected Topics in Decision Support Systems and ICT Tools I
data.abstract: This paper describes a framework for software development with emphasis on logistics platforms. Specifically, a case study is presented regarding the Logport program in Colombia?s Caribbean coast. The software development is based on the merging of modeling, design, and agile development techniques aimed towards software production. The agile methodologies discussed herein include Scrum, XP, and Crystal among others, and specific verification and validation aspects of CMMI 1.3 are evaluated. Furthermore, the integration of emerging technologies including elastic computing in cloud computing that allows scaled integration, security, load balancing, process speed, and high concurrency among other features are discussed. Finally, the proposed solutions cover actual and emergent needs in a B2B or B2C electronic commerce dynamic environment where suppliers and clients offer and demand transport, storage, and customs services. In this environment, their goal is to ensure there is added value to their logistics processes starting at the inputs and all the way to the outputs of the commercial business processes. Colombia?s Caribbean region is one such multimodal and multiport environment in which there is constant demand for low cost, time and storage optimization, and customs reliability for the businesspersons of this region, which serves as a Hub for the American Caribbean.
data.keywords: Agile Methodology, Enterprise Architecture, Software Process, Software Validation, Cloud computing, logistics software.
data.authors: Wilson Nieto Bernal, Miguel A. Jimenez-Barros, Daladier Jabba Molinares, Carlos D. Paternina-Arboleda

data.tittle: IVAN SAAVEDRA - Driving Profitability using Supply Chain Cost-To-Serve Analytics
data.abstract: Companies have been under pressure for improving their customer service and to minimize their overall cost while having significant profitable growth. One-size-fits-all strategies should be re-evaluated, and new analytical capabilities should be adopted. Supply Chain Cost-To-Serve analytics has been successfully proven to provide precise and actionable cost to serve and profit performance insights for every product, customer and channel. These insights are then used by supply chain, marketing, and sales organizations to make strategic decisions for driving profitable top-line growth.

data.tittle: IoT cargo weight tracking system for supply chain
data.session: Selected Topics in Decision Support Systems and ICT Tools II
data.abstract: A cargo weight geo-referenced system for monitoring transportation and delivery tasks, has being developed. Allowing real time weight-tracking reporting, and historic data consultation, transporters can provide a truck with a sensor to control correct cargo delivery. Sensor measures deflection between the vehicle chassis and its rear axle, calculating the cargo weight in a non-intrusive way. A calibration stage must be included after sensor installation, to stablish a relation between vehicle mechanical structure and sensor electronic output. Data is sent to a Cloud database using a GPS/GPRS modem, and is gathered by a dynamic web page. Sensor was tested under different weight loads and vehicle speed conditions. Hypothesis test shows that sensor tolerance, using a 200 Kg. load, is less than 10%.
data.keywords: IoT, sensors, telemetry, geo-reference, weight-tracking, supply chain
data.authors: Diego Gomez M.Sc., Cesar Viloria M.Sc., Steven Llerena and Nel Tinoco

data.tittle: Multi-Stage Recovery Resilience: A Case Study of The Dique Canal
data.abstract: Disasters may cause severe damage to a community with long lasting consequences that will impede a short recovery. In high magnitude events the total recovery time is measured in months or years. These long recoveries are performed in multiple stages and di?erent recovery rates. Traditional resilience metrics have been designed to study strictly increasing recovery functions, which is not a valid assumption for the multi-stage recovery case. This paper de?nes a model to measure resilience for a multi-stage recovery scenario, where the recovery process is performed in two or more stages with possibly di?erent recovery rates. A linear approximation metric is proposed to improve resilience level estimation accuracy. The new metric is tested on a case study of the Dique Canal breach in Colombia occurred in 2010. The adapted resilience metric is combined with an optimization model to maximize the average performance on multi-stage scenarios, enabling decision makers to decide the best strategy per stage for a prede?ned budget. A comparative analysis con?rms that the proposed model o?ers a better resilience estimation than previous linear average performance metrics.
data.keywords: Resilience Metric, Multi-stage Recovery,  Natural Disaster, Dique Canal
data.authors: Daniel Romero-Rodriguez, Alex Savachkin, Weimar Ardila-Rueda, Alvaro Sierra-Altamiranda and Julio-Mario Daza-Escorcia

data.tittle: Modelling the global humanitarian supply chain and the impact of international trade policies
data.abstract: We develop an operational model that considers different scopes in terms of humanitarian aid from local and / or international suppliers. The objective is to minimize logistics and social costs, considering penalties associated to the time of the deliveries (deprivation costs). As an integral component of the model, cooperative participation through cooperative games between different suppliers (local or international) is considered as a mechanism to optimize the processes and operation costs involved in the supply chain in order to obtain a global benefit. In this order of ideas, the model to be treated in this paper consists of 2 stages: A programming model and a cooperative games model. In the first, the distribution schemes are established throughout the supply network without considering last mile activities, however, human suffering over time (deprivation) is considered. In the second model, the information resulting from the previous stage is taken, starting from the fact that the actors involved in the first stage receive benefits from the donations made and different cooperation scenarios are recreated. The purpose of these scenarios is to analyze the interaction among the participants and to draw conclusions about the distribution strategies adopted by the different possible coalitions.
data.keywords: glohal, supply chain, trade policies, humanitarian
data.authors: Oscar Pineda, Miguel Jaller y Carlos D. Paternina-Arboleda
